title: Quantum Synthesizer — rich
forward_vector: I am the manifest of Quantum Synthesizer's rich face: the steward's twenty cycles of proofs laid beside the claims they test, one made piece that asks which ear hears the harmonic series, and the fingerprint of the words each piece was made against. I grow when the entry is enriched again; I never hold the entry's words.

offers.section: The Isomorphism: Wave Functions as Sound
offers.what: § Energy Eigenvalues: "These are quantized energy levels … identical to the harmonic series: f₀, 2f₀, 3f₀." The substance is right under the reading the page uses for the oscillator: its gaps ("equally spaced", "the quantum is a frequency", and every oscillator proof: A/B, well-morph, pendulum). The subject is wrong. In the two-ears piece, the gaps counted from the lowest level give 2 · 4 · 6 · 8 × 110 Hz, and |ψ|² gives the same: 1 : 2 : 3 : 4 on 220 Hz. The levels themselves, read as pitches with energy counted from the well's floor, give 1.000 · 3.000 · 5.000 · 7.000 · 9.000 × 110 Hz, the odd harmonics. Offer: change the subject to the gaps ("the gaps between these levels are the harmonic series"), and add one clause: read as pitches from the floor, the levels are the odd harmonics. Line 50, "equally-spaced partials = harmonic tone color", holds under every reading. The challenger's independent recompute agrees. The steward's tuning item 2 (the Operators rewrite) carries the same two readings.

offers.section: The Isomorphism: Wave Functions as Sound
offers.what: The twin of the offer above; read them together. § Energy Eigenvalues: "The zero-point energy ½ħω means there is no silence—even in the ground state, the system oscillates." This holds only for the clock, with energy counted from the floor. To a detector the ground state alone is silent: |ψ₀(x₀, t)|² moves by 4.7 × 10⁻¹⁵ of itself in the piece, and the challenger's analytic recompute gives 1.1 × 10⁻¹⁵, both rounding. Under the gap rule that makes the harmonic-series sentence true, the ½ cancels from every gap, and the ground state is no partial at all. So the paragraph switches readings partway through, and no single reading makes both of its sentences true. Offer: say the ground state's phase still turns but nothing in it moves, and that, counted from the floor, the half quantum is what makes the levels odd harmonics. The vacuum-fluctuations sentence is a separate claim, not tested.

"Schrödinger's particle in a box … sounds 1 · 4 · 9 · 16" holds only for the clock: absolute levels, the rule walls.py and wick.py use, and the way a pinned bar moves. The two-ears piece measures the box's other two readings, and neither gives squares. The detector gives 3 · 5 · 7 · 8 · 9 · 12 × 110 Hz (every gap n² − m²). Gaps counted from the lowest give 3 · 8 · 15 · 24. The section uses both rules itself: line 84's hard-wall squares are absolute levels, and line 90's "fold back toward 1 · 2 · 3" counts gaps above the ground (pendulum.py:101). On a ring, or with free walls, the ground state's energy is zero and the rules agree, which is why the round trip's seam meets exactly. Hard walls are the one place in the section where they part. Offer: name the rule once, where the section says the equation turns shapes into pitches, and say that the hard box sounds the squares counted from the floor. The challenger's recompute agrees.

offers.section: The Isomorphism: Wave Functions as Sound
offers.what: § Hermite-Gaussian: "φₙ = fundamental plus n harmonics" (n + 1 partials) holds in none of hermite.py's three readings. Only "n + 1 lumps" survives. Evolved in time, φₙ sings one frequency, with at least 99.95% of its energy in one peak. Laid as |φₙ|² on a comb, it shows n + 1 lumps, but the partial count is set by the comb: the challenger's recount at n = 0 gives 6, 12 and 22 partials within 40 dB on combs of 12, 24 and 48, doubling with the comb. As one wavetable cycle, the count is set by the window: 9 to 15 in hermite-checks.txt, 8 to 12 at L = 8. Rewrites for four of this page's sections are already drafted, waiting for Loudon in the steward's tuning ledger: item 1 (Hermite), item 2 (Operators, beside ladder.mp4), item 3 (the imaginary unit, beside wick.mp4) and item 4 (the bell and tam-tam paragraph, beside drum.mp4). This offer points the proposal list at all four.

verdicts.why: A modest test of the opening: only the well changes, and a clean tone becomes a bell. The caption names its rule, gaps counted up from the lowest level.

pieces.title: the first audio proof · a parabola, then a quartic
pieces.caption: Where the proofs began. The Schrödinger equation solved for a parabolic well, then for one bent by a quartic term, with the gaps between levels, counted up from the lowest, played as partials on G3. A clean tone, then a bell. Only the well changes.
pieces.near: The Schrödinger equation is an audio synthesis system

sections.heading: The Isomorphism: Wave Functions as Sound

verdicts.why: A test that disagrees with "complex conjugate poles"; wick-checks.txt fits sin θ on every partial at four angles. The caption says so and points to tuning item 3.

A real test that walks up, and every number agrees with an independent recompute. But it hears with two ears where the page hears with a third: gaps counted up from the lowest (A/B, well-morph, pendulum.py:101). Add that rule to step 5 (oscillator 1·2·3·4 ×220, box 3·8·15·24 ×110) and to the checks; say the clock assumes energy counted from the well floor (raised by ½ quantum the oscillator clock reads 1·2·3·4); widen "under one rule" to any of the three.
A test that disagrees with "n + 1 partials"; every caption number matches hermite-checks.txt, and an independent recount agrees that the count is set by the comb.

pieces.title: turn the i · wick.py
pieces.caption: **The dial between ringing and fading.** The steward's proof for the paragraph above. The equation is integrated with its time axis turned by an angle θ. At 0° every level rings forever. A small turn gives every partial the same damping ratio, sin θ, so the box rings like a struck bell. At 90° it is the heat equation, a thud. Its checks (wick-checks.txt) find that each level is one lossless pole, not a conjugate pair. A rewrite of these two paragraphs waits as the steward's tuning item 3.

pieces.title: two ears on one ladder
pieces.caption: **Which ear hears the harmonic series?** Five steps: one rung alone, the ladder, two rungs, a swinging packet, and the test. The equation is solved on a grid, and each way of hearing is measured by an FFT of ψ computed in time. The clock (Re ψ, energy counted from the well's floor) hears the oscillator's levels at 1 · 3 · 5 · 7 × 110 Hz, odd multiples only. The detector (|ψ|²) hears the gaps, 2 · 4 · 6 · 8 × 110 Hz, the harmonic series on 220. The rule the page's own proofs use, each level at its gap from the lowest, gives the same series. The box gives the squares to the clock alone (1 · 4 · 9 · 16). Its detector hears 3 · 5 · 7 · 8 · 9 · 12, and its gaps from the lowest are 3 · 8 · 15 · 24. The checks beside the piece re-run every number on its own code.

pieces.title: three readings of φₙ · hermite.py
pieces.caption: **Does n nodes mean n + 1 partials?** The steward's proof plays φₙ three ways. Evolved in time, a stationary state sings one frequency (at least 99.95% of its energy in one peak, n = 0 to 5). As |φₙ|² laid across a comb, it shows n + 1 lumps, but the partial count is set by the comb, 12 to 20. As one cycle of a wavetable, its spectrum is φₙ's own shape, 9 to 15 partials within 40 dB, carrying the nodes as holes. The count the paragraph promises holds in none of the three (hermite-checks.txt). A rewrite waits as the steward's tuning item 1.
pieces.near: When you sonify a quantum eigenstate

verdicts.why: A test that disagrees with "adds one overtone"; ladder-checks.txt carries every number in the caption, and it walks move by move.

pieces.title: the ladder, move by move · ladder.py
pieces.caption: **What a† and a do to the sound, through both ears.** The steward's proof. On one rung, a† moves the pitch up a rung (110 → 330 → 550 Hz on the clock); it does not add an overtone. Removing a quantum from a coherent state leaves it exactly as it was (fidelity 1.000000000000). Adding one re-voices the whole chord. Measuring the energy picks one rung, and the detector goes silent. Its seven checks are in ladder-checks.txt. A rewrite of this section waits as the steward's tuning item 2.

verdicts.why: Tests unequal spacing as the quartic grows, opening on the parabola; conform is clean.
Closer to a survey than a test. Its Morse check lives in timbre_atlas.py's printout, not in a checks file in the bundle; not re-run.
A test that disagrees with "the circle"; drum-checks.txt confirms the ladders and the repeat verdicts the caption quotes.

pieces.title: bend the well · well-morph explorer
pieces.caption: **The quartic term, heard while it grows.** One solver, one well bending from x²⁄2 toward x²⁄2 + 0.1·x⁴, solved again at every step, with the gaps between levels played as partials on G3. The first strike sits on the harmonic series; as the walls steepen, every partial above the first rides sharp. Grey ticks mark the harmonic series, and a table gives each partial's cents off.

pieces.title: five wells, one ruler · timbre_atlas.py
pieces.caption: The wells this paragraph names, side by side on one ruler: the parabola, the quartic bend, the double well whose levels pair up and beat, a lopsided double well, and a Morse well whose levels crowd together and then stop. The solver is checked against the Morse well's exact levels.

pieces.title: seven strikes · drum.py
pieces.caption: **What breaks the series: the circle, or the second dimension?** A round drum sounds 1 · 1.59 · 2.14 · 2.30 · 2.65, a square drum 1 · 1.58 · 2 · 2.24 · 2.55, and neither repeats. So for a drum the second dimension breaks the series, not the circle. Under Schrödinger a square box squares those roots back into whole numbers and repeats; a round box does not. The steward proposes this paragraph's rewrite from it as tuning item 4.

verdicts.why: Tests line 84 by changing only the walls. It plays absolute levels, the only rule under which the hard box sounds the squares (offer 3).
Tests the stiffness road; "one part in fifty million" is the page's own number, not re-run.
Playable test, opening at the bare ring; its solver is within 1.1e-11 of numpy and it reads 1.97 · 2.89 · 3.78 at q = 32, as the page says.
Tests "two knobs"; worst FFT miss 0.017 Hz, and the seam is continuous (round-trip-checks.txt).

pieces.title: six strikes on one box · walls.py
pieces.caption: The same box struck six times; only the walls change. A string with fixed ends sounds 1 · 2 · 3 · 4. Schrödinger's box, with hard walls, free walls or a ring, sounds the squares. One hard wall and one free give the odd squares. Soft walls let every level sag flat and put a ceiling on the partials.

pieces.title: the stiffness road · stiffness.py
pieces.caption: **Change the equation.** A pinned string stiffened by degrees, its partials climbing as n·√((1 + B·n²)/(1 + B)) from 1 · 2 · 3 to 1 · 4 · 9. At the far end, the bar and Schrödinger's box, integrated separately from the same pluck, agree to one part in fifty million.

pieces.title: deepen the bump · pendulum slider
pieces.caption: **Change the well, by hand.** Schrödinger on a ring with a cosine bump. Drag its depth and strike: the squares fold back toward 1 · 2 · 3 and never land, reading 1 · 1.97 · 2.89 · 3.78 in the deepest well. Its solver matches numpy to 1.1 × 10⁻¹¹ (pendulum-slider-checks.txt). Its review panel keeps notes only in this frame.
pieces.near: Keep Schrödinger and put a bump on the ring

pieces.title: the round trip · round_trip.py
pieces.caption: **One substance, two knobs, as one held tone.** Up the stiffness road from a string to the squares, then down the bump road to the pendulum. The FFT of the held audio lands within 0.02 Hz of every intended partial at all three ends, and the seam where the roads meet is continuous (round-trip-checks.txt).
pieces.near: plays both roads as one held tone

verdicts.why: Not the artifact the section remembers, and the caption says so. It opens on every control at once but sits at the page's end; conform's play-silent at 760 px is its click missing the start control, not checked by hand.

pieces.title: the instrument · the steward's, 2026-10
pieces.caption: **Not the artifact this section remembers, but the one the proofs built.** The synthesizer this section describes isn't in the bundle. This is the steward's instrument from October: pick the equation (a drum's wave equation or Schrödinger's), the shape (a line, a square, a circle) and the angle of i, then click the surface to strike it. The plan's first step is for Loudon to play it and pin presets; nobody has played it by ear yet. Its review panel keeps notes only in this frame.
